title: gpu-inventory-ledger-west-eu-apac-scenarios
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is an operational ledger and scenario playbook for the GPU inventory and procurement pipeline across West (us-west), EU (europe-west), and APAC (asia-east) regions. It is intended for infra planning, procurement coordination, and SRE capacity forecasting. This version focuses on SKU mix sensitivity, rolling lead-time risk, and a small experiment for mixed spot/reserved strategies.

Status summary (quick):
- Snapshot date: 2026-03-05
- Current available pool (usable for scheduling): 1,160 GPUs
- Committed (allocated to customers / reserved capacity): 920 GPUs
- Free buffer (target pool for absorbing spikes/failovers): 240 GPUs (target 200-300)
- Active POs in pipeline: 7 orders (see ledger below)

Inventory snapshot (by region and SKU) - rough table:
- us-west:
  - H100-94G: 320 available (alloc 280, free 40)
  - A100-80G: 160 available (alloc 140, free 20)
  - L4-48G: 40 available (alloc 20, free 20)
- europe-west:
  - H100-94G: 220 available (alloc 190, free 30)
  - A100-80G: 120 available (alloc 110, free 10)
- asia-east:
  - H100-94G: 200 available (alloc 170, free 30)
  - L4-48G: 100 available (alloc 100, free 0)

Key assumptions used in scenario calculations:
- Normal lead time (manufacturer -> regional DC): H100 = 12 weeks median, A100 = 8 weeks median, L4 = 6 weeks median.
- Lead time volatility window: +/- 25% for H100; +/-15% for A100; +/-20% for L4.
- Ramp-to-traffic for new models: model onboarding increases average utilization 7-12% over first 30 days after rollout.
- Target utilization ceilings by pool: Hosted API pools aim for 65% avg utilization, Dedicated pools target 75% utilization.

Active procurement ledger (outstanding POs - simplified):
- PO-2026-0112 | Vendor: CoreCompute | SKU: H100-94G x 200 | Qty shipped: 0/200 | ETA: 2026-04-20 | Lead time reported: 14 weeks | Destination: us-west | Notes: tranche 1 of 2, awaiting customs docs.
- PO-2026-0089 | Vendor: AtlasTech | SKU: A100-80G x 120 | Qty shipped: 120/120 | ETA: 2026-03-10 (arrived) | Destination: europe-west | Notes: being racked; expected live 2026-03-15.
- PO-2026-0137 | Vendor: EastWave | SKU: L4-48G x 150 | Qty shipped: 0/150 | ETA: 2026-05-05 | Destination: asia-east | Notes: incentive discount attached, conditional on payment terms.
- PO-2026-0150 | Vendor: CoreCompute | SKU: H100-94G x 100 | Qty shipped: 0/100 | ETA: 2026-06-10 | Destination: europe-west | Notes: spot/commit mixed pricing, vendor expects 16-week lead time.
- PO-2026-0168 | Vendor: BulkGPUs | SKU: A100-80G x 80 | Qty shipped: 0/80 | ETA: 2026-04-01 | Destination: us-west | Notes: expedited shipping paid.
- PO-2026-0175 | Vendor: EdgeSupply | SKU: L4-48G x 40 | Qty shipped: 0/40 | ETA: 2026-03-25 | Destination: asia-east | Notes: partial ship scheduled.
- PO-2026-0181 | Vendor: CoreCompute | SKU: H100-94G x 40 | Qty shipped: 0/40 | ETA: 2026-03-30 | Destination: us-west | Notes: replacement for DOA units.

Reorder policy (current pragmatic rules):
- Safety buffer per region = max(200 GPUs, 15% of regional peak allocated capacity) but evaluated weekly.
- Trigger reorder when free buffer < 100 GPUs regionally and projected steady-state utilization > 70% in next 4 weeks.
- Preferred SKU mix for reinforcement: H100 for Dedicated and high-throughput hosted inference; L4 for low-cost embeddings/replicas; A100 used for transitional workloads.

Scenario analysis (high level):
1) Baseline demand (next 12 weeks) - steady growth +5% workload/month:
   - Expected net need: +220 GPUs (mostly H100) across regions. Our current pipeline covers ~340 GPUs (if all POs land on ETA). Net positive margin but concentrated in us-west (risk: europe deficit).
2) Lead-time shock (+40% lead time for H100 due to capacity squeeze):
   - H100 ETA shifts: median 17 weeks -> some POs slip into Q3. Europe-west shows shortfall of ~80 H100 GPUs by June. Recommended mitigations: re-route A100 bursts from us-west to europe-west transiently; negotiate local short-term rentals (1-3 month) or convert some A100 orders to H100 where vendor allows swap.
3) Demand spike (new enterprise customer onboarding expected month 6 with 200 GPU committed Dedicated):
   - If onboarding accelerated, need to reserve 200 GPUs in europe-west or commit to cross-region failover. Evaluate Dedicated win vs ability to deliver SLA. Consider delaying non-critical capacity refresh by 6 weeks to free allocation.
4) Spot availability experiment (us-west pools):
   - Proposal: convert 10% of idle pool to spot-backed nodes (preemptible instances / small retailers) for non-latency critical workloads. Expected savings 18% on those jobs, risk of 20% preemption events. Controlled rollout recommended for 8-week trial.

Sensitivity matrix (short):
- +10% utilization -> buffer erosion of ~70 GPUs / month if no replenishment.
- +25% H100 lead time -> single-region shortfall of 60-100 GPUs by month 4.
- Converting 50 A100 -> H100 (vendor swap) increases procurement cost ~12% but reduces cross-compatibility headaches; useful if H100 demand is sticky.

Operational notes and friction points observed recently:
- Customs clearance for Europe orders added variable 5-12 days; local broker engagement improved processing time in last quarter.
- Vendor invoicing mismatch: two POs (AtlasTech and EdgeSupply) had invoice SKUs not matching RMA tags; blocked payment until corrected.
- Rack-space constraint in europe-west DC: 3U shelves are almost full; need to confirm spare PDUs and heavy-lift schedule before next bulk arrive.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Approve swap authority for procurement team: allow up to 40% (by value) of an upcoming A100 order to be swapped to H100 within 5 business days of ETD change? (decision owner: procurement lead)
- Short-term rental budget: approve up to $180k CAPEX for 1-3 month rental contracts for europe-west to cover lead-time volatility?
- Spot experiment sign-off: SRE + CostOps to confirm rollback plan and SLA impacts.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Procurement: confirm customs docs for PO-2026-0112 and push for air-bridge option if delay >14 days. (owner: Daniel)
- [ ] SRE: map cross-region failover window for Dedicated customers (europe->us-west) and quantify latency/SLO impact. (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Finance: release final payment to AtlasTech once invoice corrected; reconcile with warehouse receiving. (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Infra ops: validate power/space in europe-west DC for additional 100 H100s (owner: Hannah)

Appendix - quick heuristics for SKU choice (operational):
- H100: use for high-throughput, long-context workloads and Dedicated pools where customer cost sensitivity less.
- A100: fallback for medium throughput tasks; use for model training and inference where cost/perf tradeoff still reasonable.
- L4: embeddings and lightweight shards; good for scaling many small workloads cheaply.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and contains some rough numbers for planning. Please flag any PO/ETA mismatches in linked_artifacts. If you have local sales commitments that change demand assumptions, add a line in the comment thread and tag the author.

History and provenance:
- Drafted by Sofia Martinez (eng-infrastructure) 2026-01-20. Updated with ETA changes and rack constraints 2026-03-05.

End of ledger.
